title: The sanctuary (Gaudium et Spes 16)
hook: conscience is the most secret core and sanctuary of a person
tomorrow: who shows you what a human being is meant to be?

segments.voice: Yesterday Gaudium et Spes opened on everyone's joys and griefs, the afflicted first, and said nothing human is foreign to Christ's followers.

Something broke, and it's your call whether to say so. The group chat has an opinion. A search bar has an opinion. Somebody's video, with good lighting, has an opinion. Then it's late, the phone is face down on the nightstand, and there's one voice left, the one nobody else can hear. The same council document gives the place that voice speaks a church name. It calls it a sanctuary.
screen: `EVERY FEED HAS AN OPINION.` → `THE PHONE, FACE DOWN.` → `ONE VOICE LEFT.`

segments.voice: Paragraph sixteen starts deep inside a person. There, it says, each of us finds a law we didn't write for ourselves, and still have to obey. Its voice keeps calling us to love what is good and avoid what is evil, and when it matters it speaks plainly: do this, shun that. The council says this law is written by God in the human heart, an echo of Paul's letter to the Romans, and that obeying it is the very dignity of a person. Then the image. Conscience, it says, is the most secret core and sanctuary of a person, where they are alone with God, whose voice echoes in their depths. In a church, the sanctuary is the holy space around the altar. The council puts one inside every human being. So conscience isn't the same as a mood, or whatever feels least stressful at midnight. It's a law you didn't invent, heard honestly. And the council is careful. Conscience can get things wrong. When it errs out of an ignorance a person couldn't overcome, it keeps its dignity. It's different when someone stops caring what is true and good, or when a habit of sin slowly dims it. So the paragraph asks two things at once: listen to that voice, and keep it clear. It adds that being faithful to conscience joins Christians with everyone else searching for what is true.
screen: `A LAW WE DIDN'T WRITE.` · `THE SANCTUARY INSIDE.` · `NOT A MOOD: A VOICE HEARD HONESTLY.` · `LISTEN, AND KEEP IT CLEAR.` · then, large: `ALONE WITH GOD.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and bring one choice in front of you to mind, even a small one. Let the other voices go quiet, one at a time, and ask only: what is the good thing here? Then wait, and listen.
The sanctuary. Gaudium et Spes's name for conscience: the inmost place where a person is alone with God.
Pocket this one: alone with God, where a law you didn't write still speaks plainly. Rest well.

screen: `DAY 1587 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: WHO SHOWS YOU WHAT A HUMAN IS MEANT TO BE?`

howItsDone: Catholics are taught to form their conscience and follow it, and many examine their conscience in quiet before confession or at the end of the day.

pairs: not written by us, still obeyed
where a person is alone with God

myth: conscience is just the guilty feeling after you do something wrong
the council calls it a law we didn't write, calling us to good before we act.
Gaudium et Spes says conscience can err and still keep its dignity
when it errs from an ignorance a person couldn't overcome.
following conscience sets Christians apart from everyone else

fork.setup: at your part-time job, the manager says to mark yesterday's pastries as fresh. everyone else does it. by Gaudium et Spes 16, where does the decision get made?
options: in the sanctuary: alone with God, asking what is good.
with the coworkers: if everyone does it, it's fine.
with the manager: an order takes away your part in it.
fork.reveal: the council puts the decision in conscience, the sanctuary where a person is alone with God and hears a law they didn't write: do good, avoid evil.

chat.says: Lupe broke Abuela's Guadalupe statue and begged me not to tell. Mia says follow your heart. which?
options: Conscience isn't just a mood. Get quiet, ask what's good here, then help Lupe tell Abuela herself.
Follow your heart. Whatever feels least stressful right now is probably what conscience wants.
Just do what Abuela would want. Grown-ups' rules decide what's right, so it isn't on you.
chat.meaning: Gaudium et Spes 16: conscience hears a law we didn't write, calling us to the good. It's where a person is alone with God, not just a feeling.

Gaudium et Spes.meaning: Vatican II's document on the Church in the modern world

sanctuary.meaning: in a church, the holy space around the altar

Romans.meaning: Paul's letter to the Christians in Rome, in the New Testament

conscience.meaning: the inner judgment that calls a person to do good and avoid evil

sources.work: Second Vatican Council, Gaudium et Spes
The Bible (Douay-Rheims), echoed in the paragraph

notes: Paraphrased from GS 16: the law not self-imposed, love good and avoid evil, 'do this, shun that', written by God in the heart, obeying it is human dignity, conscience as the most secret core and sanctuary where one is alone with God, fidelity to conscience joining Christians with others in seeking truth, invincible ignorance vs. carelessness and habitual sin.
